content.value_statement: Teams need repeatable guidance when creating Claude Code skills, triggers, and guardrails. This skill gives structured rules, examples, and troubleshooting steps for safer skill development.
actual_capabilities: Explains the structure of Claude Code skill files and frontmatter.
Shows how to configure keyword, intent, file path, and content triggers.
Documents hook behavior for UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, and Stop events.
Provides testing checklists for new skills and trigger changes.
Troubleshoots activation problems, false positives, hook registration, and performance issues.
Summarizes progressive disclosure and the 500-line guidance for skill content.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not install hooks or modify projects by itself.
It focuses on Claude Code skill systems and may not fit unrelated agent frameworks.
Some examples reference project-local .claude paths that users must adapt.
Manual testing is still required before enforcing blocking guardrails.

use_cases.title: Create a Team Skill
use_cases.description: Draft a new skill with clear frontmatter, trigger terms, and reference files.

use_cases.title: Tune Guardrail Rules
use_cases.description: Refine blocking or suggested rules to reduce false positives while preserving important checks.

use_cases.title: Debug Skill Activation
use_cases.description: Trace why a skill did not trigger, why a hook did not run, or why a rule blocked work.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Claude Code skill plan for [topic]. Include the skill name, description, trigger keywords, and required reference files.

prompt_templates.title: Write Trigger Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me define keyword, intent, file path, and content triggers for a skill that handles [workflow]. Explain likely false positives.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Guardrail
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this guardrail design for [risk]. Check the enforcement level, block message, skip conditions, and testing checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Hook Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Troubleshoot why my Claude Code skill hook did not activate. Ask for the prompt, edited file path, trigger rules, and hook output.

output_examples.input: I need a new skill for database query safety.
output_examples.output: A skill plan with a focused name, trigger strategy, guardrail level, reference files, and a validation checklist.

output_examples.input: My frontend skill triggers on too many prompts.
output_examples.output: A tuning review that narrows keywords, improves intent patterns, adds file exclusions, and lists regression tests.

output_examples.input: The hook does not block edits when expected.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting path that checks hook registration, file matches, content matches, session state, and skip settings.

best_practices: Keep main skill files concise and move detailed guidance into direct reference files.
Test each trigger with positive and negative examples before enabling blocking enforcement.
Use block enforcement only for risks that justify interrupting the edit workflow.
anti_patterns: Do not use broad trigger words that match ordinary development prompts.
Do not hide critical instructions in deeply nested reference files.
Do not add permanent skip markers without a clear verification reason.

faq.question: Does this skill create files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides the agent or user through skill design, configuration, testing, and troubleshooting.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code support, with content focused on Claude Code skills.

faq.question: Can it help reduce false positives?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to narrow keywords, intent patterns, file paths, and content rules.

faq.question: Does it include hook internals?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, Stop hooks, exit codes, and session state behavior.

faq.question: Is it suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. It starts with basic skill structure and links to deeper reference material for advanced topics.

faq.question: What should users verify before publishing a skill?
faq.answer: They should validate syntax, test trigger coverage, check false positives, and confirm enforcement level choices.
